meta.title: WS v6 milestone 2
meta.subtitle: The Rust daemon `wsd` replaces the zsh `ws` on one machine. Loop run `loop-ws-v6-local-2026-10-16-210924`, merge gate of milestone 2.

summary: `ws` runs on a Rust daemon (`wsd`) instead of zsh scripts and lock files. The daemon owns sessions, logs, messages, dependency edges, triggers and a local MCP server. It runs Loop runners as ws sessions. Command names, flags, output and exit codes stay the same. `ws backend zsh` is the way back. 35 work phases and 1 review phase. 186 files, +33858/-749. The ws shell suite: 1013 tests passed.

tldr.changed: `ws` runs on one Rust daemon, `wsd`, instead of zsh scripts and lock files. Commands, flags, output and exit codes stay the same.
tldr.lookFirst: Change 6, Messages: delivery moved from the file inbox to log events with acknowledgement.
tldr.risk: medium; `ws backend zsh` switches back while the daemon runs, and 1 major finding (F4) waits for Phase 71.

changes.how: One `ws` binary: CLI, `ws daemon`, `ws mcp`. Cargo workspace `wsd/`, 3 crates.
changes.why: One process owns all state. No shell lock files. Later milestones (telemetry, hub, sync) extend it.

changes.how: Append-only, hash-chained log per session. The SQLite registry is a projection that can be rebuilt from the logs.
changes.why: The log is the source of truth: replay, audit, later sync between machines. The registry is a disposable index.

changes.how: ULID per session plus the `#N` alias.
changes.why: ULIDs are unique across devices (v6 sync). Aliases keep the user commands.

changes.how: Typed lifecycle state machine, tmux driver, headless supervisor with process groups. A daemon restart re-adopts running children.
changes.why: Sessions survive a closed terminal and a daemon restart. A stop waits for the real exit.

changes.how: One `prepare` function builds argv, environment and hook files for every Claude, Codex or Grok launch. Loop runners use it through `ws agent prepare`.
changes.why: Hooks, MCP and milestone 3 telemetry come from one place.

changes.how: Log events: sent, delivered, read. Delivery at the agent Stop hook, or by paste when idle, with retries and acknowledgement. A message to a finished session reopens it.
changes.why: Confirmed delivery. The order survives a crash. Replaces the file inbox.

changes.how: Dependency edges, `ws done`, `ws wait`, `ws on … done --spawn/--send-to` triggers as edge actions in the log.
Local stdio server, 12 tools (`session_*`, `wait`, `loop_*`, `phase_spawn`). Added to each agent launch through flags. Caller identity from `WS_SESSION_ID`. Spawn limits (children, depth).
changes.why: Agents drive ws directly. No edits to Claude or Codex config files. The caller cannot be faked.

changes.how: Runners run as ws headless sessions when wsd answers. Otherwise they launch directly. `ws top`, `ws loop start/stop`. Review worktrees belong to a session and are removed after it.
changes.why: Loop runs are visible and controllable in ws. The picker shows no review worktrees.

changes.how: The fzf picker and tmux bindings read data from Rust commands.
`./install.sh ws` builds `~/.ws/bin/ws-rs` and installs LaunchAgent `com.rstagi.wsd` with KeepAlive.
changes.why: The daemon always runs. launchd restarts it after a crash.

changes.how: Backend file `~/.ws/backend` (rust or zsh). Both backends share the alias lock. Import of zsh state. `ws backend zsh` returns to zsh.
changes.why: Live state migrates with a safe rollback. Phase 54 removes the zsh code in milestone 3.

changes.how: Golden tests from the zsh suite, written before each port.
changes.why: Habits, scripts and the ws-sessions skill keep working.

changes.how: One lane, TDD, sandboxed tests (temporary HOME, private tmux sockets), max-tier review.
changes.why: Parallel lanes conflict on `Cargo.lock`. Sandboxes protect live state.

delivered.criterion: Stale-socket tests are not flaky, two daemons cannot both replace the socket, and CLAUDE.md names the Rust and spike checks (milestone 1 findings F1, F2, F4).
delivered.result: Socket flock and a shared daemon fixture, a stale-socket helper child, CLAUDE.md Rust and spike commands.

delivered.criterion: Log entries carry the v6 §3 fields in a hash chain with fsync, no `seq` gaps, tamper detection and a reported truncated last line. `ws init` writes the device identity.
delivered.result: Append-only hash-chained session log, device identity, `ws init`.

delivered.criterion: A SQLite projection of the logs that `rebuild` regenerates, `#N` aliases from a floor, and a resolver for alias, name or ULID prefix.
delivered.result: SQLite registry projection, rebuild from logs, aliases and resolver.

delivered.criterion: Typed session states with errors for illegal transitions, a lifecycle API, a `session.<state>` event per transition and the caller recorded per call.
delivered.result: Typed lifecycle transitions and a session lifecycle API with caller audit.

delivered.criterion: A tmux driver for sessions, windows, panes, `@ws_*` options, bracketed paste, capture and pane death, tested on a sandbox server.
delivered.result: tmux driver and O_CLOFORK lock files (an L3 fix for inherited flock descriptors).

delivered.criterion: `ws whoami`, `ws name`, `ws sessions` and `ws show` match the zsh output (ids as `#N`) and accept `--json`.
delivered.result: Ported with `--json` and zsh golden fixtures, plus a rename API.

delivered.criterion: `ws new`, `ws add` and `ws list` work from the registry and never scan `$WS_ROOT/*/*`.
delivered.result: `ws new/add/list` on the registry with no `WS_ROOT` scan, repo setup, conductor includes and the tmux session.

delivered.criterion: `ws rm`, `ws open`, `ws pin` and bare `ws` match zsh. `ws rm` refuses a dirty worktree. Pins persist.
delivered.result: `ws rm/open/pin/attach` on the registry, dirty-worktree refusal, persisted pins, golden tests.

delivered.criterion: `ws merge` and its popup match zsh, and the `merge.test.sh` scenarios pass as Rust tests.
delivered.result: Ported, with the merge scenarios as Rust integration tests (fake gh, bare origin).

delivered.criterion: One preparation contract builds every agent launch, and `ws claude|codex|grok` start agents in tmux windows with hook settings.
delivered.result: Shared `prepare()` contract, tracked launches with hook settings, slots and resume.

delivered.criterion: `ws hook` keeps the seq/turn order, appends turn, tool and agent events, spools when the daemon is down, and keeps p95 under 50 ms on the full ingest path.
delivered.result: Ordered seq/turn, turn, tool and agent events in the session log, spool and replay, bounded tmux lookup, p95 under 50 ms.

delivered.criterion: terminal-notifier, osascript and boringnotch fire on the same hook states with the same text. `WS_NOTIFY=0` turns them off.
delivered.result: Notification adapters on hook states, `WS_NOTIFY=0`, `_dismiss`, `_build-notifier`.

delivered.criterion: `ws session create --headless` runs a command in its own process group with the given cwd, environment and I/O files.
delivered.result: Headless session supervisor and I/O contract. Notification tests wait for events. The p95 assertion became opt-in (20/20 Verify).

delivered.criterion: `phase.spawn` creates a headless child, stops it at `max_runtime`, and the daemon re-adopts a running child after a restart.
delivered.result: `phase.spawn` API, durable pid and process group, restart adoption, `max_runtime` TERM then KILL.

delivered.criterion: A stop sends SIGTERM to the process group, SIGKILL after a grace period, and returns only when the group is gone. `ws session run` waits in the foreground.
delivered.result: Headless stop waits for the process-group exit (TERM, 10 s grace, KILL). `ws session run` runs in the foreground.

delivered.criterion: `ws agent prepare --mode headless` prints the contract output, and `ws hook` accepts events with no tmux pane.
delivered.result: `ws agent prepare --mode headless` (json or sh), pane-less hooks keyed by `WS_SESSION_ID` with a durable seq/turn order.

delivered.criterion: `ws send` appends `message.sent`, the inbox is a projection, and `ws inbox` and `ws ack` work.
delivered.result: `message.sent` and `message.read` log events, a human session, an ordered inbox projection, `ws send/inbox/ack`.

delivered.criterion: The Stop hook reply blocks with the undelivered batch, and each delivery and implicit read is a log event.
delivered.result: Stop-hook batch delivery, `message.delivered` after the stdout confirm, implicit read, spool replay dedup, local-device-only injection.

delivered.criterion: Idle windows get a bracketed paste, acknowledged by the next prompt, with a requeue on timeout from an in-daemon retry worker.
delivered.result: Idle paste delivery, `UserPromptSubmit` receipt, retry worker with an acknowledgement timeout, crash-durable batches.

delivered.criterion: A message to a finished session reopens the agent in a new window, then delivers.
delivered.result: The agent reopens (`claude --resume` / `codex resume`) before delivery. The legacy `--force` is accepted.

delivered.criterion: Dependency edges as log events with cycle rejection, `ws done --output`, exit events and an event-driven `ws wait`.
delivered.result: Edge events with cycle rejection, `ws done --output`, exit events, event-driven `ws wait` API.

delivered.criterion: `ws on … done|exit --send-to/--spawn` stores one-shot edge actions in the owner log, with no lock files.
delivered.result: One-shot trigger actions in the owner log, `ws triggers`, `ws on --rm`, no lock files.

delivered.criterion: `ws migrate --from-zsh [--dry-run]` snapshots `$WS_HOME` under the zsh locks and imports sessions, logs and messages.
delivered.result: zsh importer with a snapshot under the zsh fcntl locks, a resumable journal, an alias floor and requeued pending messages.

delivered.criterion: Active triggers, branch workspaces and pins import, with trigger offsets translated to the new log.
delivered.result: Pending triggers with translated event offsets, listed branch workspaces and pins.

delivered.criterion: `ws mcp` serves the session tools over stdio, records the caller, and matches the `--json` output of each command.
delivered.result: Local stdio MCP server (10 tools in this phase), caller audit through `WS_SESSION_ID`, JSON parity with the CLI.

delivered.criterion: Every agent launch gets the `ws` MCP server through flags only, and the daemon enforces child and depth limits.
delivered.result: MCP in Claude and Codex launches with no config edits, configurable spawn limits (429 on `max_children` or `max_depth`).

delivered.criterion: `loop-runner.sh` runs each runner through `ws session run` when the Rust daemon answers, and launches directly otherwise.
delivered.result: Loop engines and the orchestrator run as ws headless sessions when wsd answers ping. Direct launch otherwise.

delivered.criterion: Timeout, pause and note watchdogs stop the runner through `ws session stop` and wait for its exit before a retry.
delivered.result: Watchdogs stop ws runner groups through wsd and wait for the exit before a retry. The direct path is unchanged.

delivered.criterion: `ws top` opens `loop-top.mjs` for the session's loop, and `loop.start` / `loop.stop` exist as API, CLI and MCP calls.
delivered.result: `ws top`, `loop.start` and `loop.stop` (API, CLI, MCP). The spool p95 assertion is opt-in through `WS_ASSERT_LATENCY`.

delivered.criterion: `ws phase worktree` creates a session-owned detached worktree that the daemon removes when the session ends. `pr-review` uses it.
delivered.result: Session-owned review worktrees with cleanup on finish or failure and restart recovery. `pr-review` uses them, with a tmp fallback.

delivered.criterion: The picker data commands print the zsh formats from the registry only.
delivered.result: Registry-backed `_rows`, `_summary`, `_preview`, `_toggle_sessions` and `_unread` with zsh golden parity tests.

delivered.criterion: `ws pick` keeps fzf and the tmux bindings, and every data command it calls is Rust.
delivered.result: The fzf picker and tmux bindings call the Rust data commands. The zsh data functions moved to `picker-legacy.sh`.

delivered.criterion: `install.sh ws` builds the release binary, copies it to `~/.ws/bin/ws-rs` and installs `com.rstagi.wsd` with KeepAlive.
delivered.result: `rust` package as a `ws` dependency, release build to `ws-rs`, KeepAlive LaunchAgent, CLI autostart when launchd does not own the socket.

delivered.criterion: The backend file `~/.ws/backend` selects zsh or rust, `ws backend` switches it under a lock, and Rust does not inject messages under zsh.
delivered.result: Durable backend selector, switch under a lock, shared alias counter lock, delivery suppressed in zsh mode, incremental import on return.

delivered.criterion: With no backend file the dispatcher selects rust, the daemon imports the zsh state once at first start, and the docs describe the Rust commands and the way back.
delivered.result: Rust is the default backend, one-time import at startup, README, CLAUDE.md and the ws-sessions skill updated.

delivered.criterion: Every participating PR has a non-blocking review verdict, and the human checks the v6 phase 1 checkpoint by hand before the merge.
delivered.result: The final review is COMMENT (non-blocking). The hand checks are the hand-test list on this page.

deviations.planned: Phase 38: install first (`./install.sh ws`), then `ws migrate --from-zsh --dry-run`, then the real import.
deviations.actual: The dry run comes before the install. There is no separate import step.
deviations.reason: `./install.sh ws` starts the daemon (`install.sh:483`), and the daemon imports the zsh state at its first start (`wsd/crates/ws-daemon/src/lib.rs:76`). After that, a dry run only returns the stored plan (`import/mod.rs:84`).

deviations.planned: Phase 19: a test measures the hook-ingest latency, and its p95 stays under 50 ms.
deviations.actual: The p95 assertions run only when `WS_ASSERT_LATENCY` is set (Phases 21 and 32).
deviations.reason: The repository Verify failed at random under load (Phase 21 HIL). The final review found the gates still inconsistent (F6, F7).

deviations.planned: Milestone 3 has no phase for the milestone 2 review findings.
deviations.actual: Phase 71 joins milestone 3 to fix F4.
deviations.reason: `ws new --agent` can fail under load with `can't find window: @N`. A retry works, so the fix waits for milestone 3.

setbacks.title: Merged-tree Verify failed after a clean runner Verify
setbacks.what: a1 (codex `gpt-6.1-sol`) passed its runner Verify. The loop then moved Phase 13 to the escalate chain: a2 ran on `claude-fable-5-1`. Cause (a2 `status.json`): a child that another test thread spawns during a fork keeps the flock file description until exec, so `try_lock` failed for about 20 ms.
setbacks.resolution: a2 opens `device.lock`, `sessions.lock` and the socket lock with `O_CLOFORK` (`ws_core::lockfile::open_lock_file`) and adds a fork-based test. 20 of 20 `cargo test -p ws-daemon --lib` runs passed.
setbacks.lesson: Open lock files with `O_CLOFORK` when tests spawn children from parallel threads.

setbacks.title: Verify failed under machine load
setbacks.what: a1 (codex) and a3 (`claude-fable-5-1`, escalate chain) claimed done, then the runner Verify failed in the notifications tests. a2 passed its runner Verify, but the merged-tree Verify failed (`phase.escalate`: notifications regression, merge reset unpushed).
setbacks.resolution: The loop escalated to Fable at a3. After a3 failed again, the orchestrator raised a HIL.

setbacks.title: HIL: tests flaky under load
setbacks.what: The notifications tests and the S5 p95 latency test passed alone, but failed in about half of the full Verify runs. Other loops kept the load average at 6 to 9. The orchestrator could not prove whether Phase 21 added a regression (HIL brief).
setbacks.resolution: Option B: make the tests deterministic first. a4 and a5 replaced the 3 s wall-clock waits with an adapter FIFO signal, made the `tmux.rs` p95 assertion opt-in (`WS_ASSERT_LATENCY=1`) and gated the F7 fake TUI on a file. a6 reported 20 consecutive full Verify passes.
setbacks.lesson: Make tests wait for an event, not for a wall-clock budget, when several loops share one machine.

setbacks.title: Two questions at the 30-minute checkpoint
setbacks.what: a4 asked whether it may fix the F7 test in `ws/tests/send.test.sh`, outside the phase Touches. a5 asked whether it may watch the detached 20-run Verify loop and hand off at 20 passes.
setbacks.resolution: The orchestrator answered yes to both (`answer.md` in each run directory). a6 finished the phase.

setbacks.title: Question at the checkpoint: repair a zsh FIFO test
setbacks.what: a1 asked whether to repair the existing zsh FIFO test before it ran the repository Verify again.
setbacks.resolution: The orchestrator answered no (`answers/p28-a1-answer.md`): the test is outside the phase Touches, and the failures came from the environment, not from Phase 28.

setbacks.title: Codex usage limit
setbacks.what: a2 (codex resume) hit the usage limit, and the model chain ended with exit 40. a3 hit the limit on `codex:@sol` and ran on `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
setbacks.resolution: The loop waited (backoff), then retried. a4 ran on codex `gpt-6.1-sol` again.

setbacks.title: Agent test failed in Verify
setbacks.what: a3 claimed done, then Verify failed in `cargo test -p ws --test agents` (1 test failed).
setbacks.resolution: a4 (commit 13f99a4) extended the test helper deadline to 30 seconds. The agent suite passed five consecutive runs.

setbacks.title: Review round 1 needed a fix
setbacks.what: The round 1 reviewer (GPT) returned `NEEDS_CHANGES`, and the critic (Claude) agreed.
setbacks.resolution: The Opus fixer pushed fix1. Round 2 reviewed the new head.

setbacks.title: Round 2 ended disputed
setbacks.what: Round 2 reached the inner cap without agreement: the critic (Grok) answered `DISAGREE_EVIDENCE` two times. F1 to F7 stayed unresolved.
setbacks.resolution: The final Opus reviewer checked each finding against the code and posted COMMENT: 1 major (F4, deferred to Phase 71) and 6 minor.

validation.command: { [ ! -f wsd/Cargo.toml ] || (cd wsd && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo build && cargo test); } && zsh tests/run.sh

findings.title: `ws new --agent` and `ws add --agent` can fail with `can't find window: @N` under load.
findings.fix: Run the command again. Phase 71 (milestone 3) fixes it.

findings.title: An interrupted test run does not clean up.
A leftover test daemon can reach the default tmux server.
`tests/run.sh` does not name the failed suites.
The latency-assertion gates are not consistent.
The latency-assertion gates are not consistent.

handTest.title: Check out the PR head
handTest.command: git -C ~/dotfile fetch origin && git -C ~/dotfile switch --detach origin/feat/wsd-local-daemon
handTest.why: The installer builds from `~/dotfile/wsd`, so the PR code must be in `~/dotfile`.

handTest.title: Back up the zsh state (optional)
handTest.why: The zsh `ws` keeps sessions, triggers and pins under `~/.ws` (`ws/lib/triggers.sh:3`, `ws/ws.sh:90`). The importer reads the same three paths.

handTest.title: Preview the import before the install
handTest.command: cd ~/dotfile/wsd && cargo build --release && ./target/release/ws migrate --from-zsh --dry-run | jq '{sessions:(.sessions|length), triggers:(.triggers|length), workspaces:(.workspaces|length), alias_floor}'
handTest.why: A dry run returns before the state store opens, so it writes nothing. Run it before step 4: after the first import, a dry run only returns the stored plan (`import/mod.rs:84`).
handTest.expect: The counts match your zsh sessions, triggers and workspaces.

handTest.title: Install, which starts the daemon and imports
handTest.why: The install kickstarts the LaunchAgent. At its first start the daemon imports the zsh state (`wsd/crates/ws-daemon/src/lib.rs:76`, `import/mod.rs:59`). `install.sh` is at the repository root, so leave `wsd/` first.
handTest.expect: The dry run lists the `ws` package and its `rust` dependency (`install.sh:19`).

handTest.title: Check the daemon and the import
handTest.command:
launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.rstagi.wsd | grep state
jq .complete ~/.ws/state/import-zsh.json
ws sessions
handTest.why: The import sets `complete` in `import-zsh.json` (`import/mod.rs:30`) after the last session. Each imported session keeps its `#N` alias (`import/mod.rs:261`).
handTest.expect: `state = running`, then `true`, then the same sessions with the same `#N`. The daemon log is `~/.ws/daemon.log`.

handTest.title: Send a message and read the inbox
handTest.command:
ws send '#N' "hi"
# in the tab of #N:
ws inbox
ws ack
handTest.why: An idle agent gets a paste (`delivery.rs:216`). A busy one gets the batch at its Stop hook (`delivery.rs:564`). A finished one reopens first (`bus.rs:162`). `ws inbox` and `ws ack` act on the current session (`cmd/inbox.rs:7`).
handTest.expect: `ws send` exits 75 (queued), also on success (`cmd/send.rs:28`). The `ws` picker opens and lists the sessions.

handTest.title: Drive ws from an agent through MCP
handTest.command:
ws claude
# ask: use session_list, session_create (headless echo hi), wait, session_tail, session_send
# then repeat with: ws codex
handTest.why: Each launch adds the `ws` MCP server through `--mcp-config` (`agents/mod.rs:93`). The tools are in `wsd/crates/ws/src/mcp/mod.rs:250-267`. In Claude they show as `mcp__ws__session_list` and so on.

handTest.title: Run a handoff with no lock files
handTest.command:
find ~/.ws -name '*.lock' | sort > /tmp/ws-locks.before
ws on <A> done --spawn claude "<prompt>"
# in session A:
ws done
ws triggers
find ~/.ws -name '*.lock' | sort | diff /tmp/ws-locks.before -
handTest.why: A trigger fires once, then the daemon removes it (`triggers.rs:263`). The daemon creates its own lock files at start, so take the baseline here and not before step 4.
handTest.expect: The child starts. `ws triggers` is empty. The diff is empty.

handTest.title: Restart the daemon under a headless session
handTest.command:
ws session create --headless -- sleep 600
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.rstagi.wsd
ws session get <ULID> | jq -r .state
handTest.why: At start the daemon adopts children that still run. `ws sessions` never shows `running` for a headless session (`cmd/sessions.rs:27`), so read the state with `ws session get`. The `--` is required (`cmd/session.rs:98`).

handTest.title: Merge PR #15, then update ~/dotfile
handTest.command:
git -C ~/dotfile switch main && git -C ~/dotfile pull --ff-only
# only when main differs from 13929c8:
cd ~/dotfile && ./install.sh ws
handTest.why: `ws-rs` is a copy of the build output, so a pull alone does not update it.

handTest.title: Resume the Loop and watch it
handTest.why: `ws top` runs `loop-top.mjs` for the loop of the current session (`cmd/top.rs:27`). Close the terminal, then reattach: the sessions survive.
handTest.expect: `ws top` shows the loop live. The picker shows no Loop or review worktrees.

rollback.step: Switch back to zsh while the daemon runs. `ws backend` posts to the daemon, so run it before you stop the daemon.
Stop the daemon. It starts again at the next login, because the plist keeps `RunAtLoad`.
To return to Rust, install again first, then select rust. The switch imports what zsh created in the meantime.
